acceptedAnswer.text:
How do Denver-area seasonal climate conditions affect drywall finishing in kitchens?
In the Denver metro area, indoor humidity levels drop significantly during winter, while summer days can bring rapid thermal shifts. In dry winter months, joint compound can dry on the surface before bonding properly underneath if a home is over-heated, leading to shrinkage or hairline cracks. Maintaining steady indoor temperatures between 55 and 70 degrees and avoiding direct forced-air heaters blowing directly onto wet mud ensures predictable curing. This temperature control helps Denver, Centennial, and Parker homeowners avoid seam flashing and joint cracking later on.
acceptedAnswer.description: Dry winter air and temperature fluctuations can cause joint compound to dry unevenly; keeping consistent indoor temperatures ensures proper curing and prevents cracks.
